title: Psalm 147: The Most High Gathers the Outcasts of Israel
body:
Read the chapter → [Psalms 147](/bible/psalms/147)

This portion of the "4 Chapters a Day" session covers [Psalms 147](/bible/psalms/147) through 150, the final psalms. All four chapters run on the same thread: praising the Most High and understanding who His people are. [Psalm 147](/bible/psalms/147) shows the Most High building up Jerusalem and gathering the outcasts of Israel from the four corners of the earth, taking pleasure in them that fear Him, and giving His word and judgments to Israel alone. [Psalm 148](/bible/psalms/148) calls all of creation to praise Him and exalts the horn of His people. [Psalm 149](/bible/psalms/149) puts the high praises of the Most High in the mouth of the saints, the children of Israel, with a two-edged sword in their hand to execute vengeance. [Psalm 150](/bible/psalms/150) closes with every living thing that hath breath praising the Most High.

**[Psalm 147:1-11](/bible/psalms/147#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/psalms/147#v1)</sup> Praise ye the Lord: for it is good to sing praises unto our God; for it is pleasant; and praise is comely.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/psalms/147#v2)</sup> The Lord doth build up Jerusalem: he gathereth together the outcasts of Israel.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/psalms/147#v3)</sup> He healeth the broken in heart, and bindeth up their wounds.
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/psalms/147#v4)</sup> He telleth the number of the stars; he calleth them all by their names.
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/psalms/147#v5)</sup> Great is our Lord, and of great power: his understanding is infinite.
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/psalms/147#v6)</sup> The Lord lifteth up the meek: he casteth the wicked down to the ground.
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/psalms/147#v7)</sup> Sing unto the Lord with thanksgiving; sing praise upon the harp unto our God:
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/psalms/147#v8)</sup> Who covereth the heaven with clouds, who prepareth rain for the earth, who maketh grass to grow upon the mountains.
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/psalms/147#v9)</sup> He giveth to the beast his food, and to the young ravens which cry.
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/psalms/147#v10)</sup> He delighteth not in the strength of the horse: he taketh not pleasure in the legs of a man.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/psalms/147#v11)</sup> The Lord taketh pleasure in them that fear him, in those that hope in his mercy.

- Praise ye the Most High, for it is good to sing praises unto our God, for it is pleasant and praise is comely. The Most High doth build up Jerusalem; He gathereth together the outcasts of Israel.
- In church they talk a lot about the outcasts of Israel being Gentiles and things of that nature, but this shows plainly that Israel are the people being gathered. Our people are going to be gathered from many different places, from the four corners of the earth, from Assyria, Hamath, Egypt, and Cush. Our people are in Israel, in India, in Arabia, and all over the world.
  - **[Isaiah 11:11-12](/bible/isaiah/11#v11)**
    > <sup>[11](/bible/isaiah/11#v11)</sup> And it shall come to pass in that day, that the Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people, which shall be left, from Assyria, and from Egypt, and from Pathros, and from Cush, and from Elam, and from Shinar, and from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea.
    >
    > <sup>[12](/bible/isaiah/11#v12)</sup> And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.

    The Most High sets His hand the second time to recover the remnant of His people from Assyria, Egypt, Pathros, Cush, Elam, Shinar, Hamath, and the islands of the sea, assembling the outcasts of Israel and the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.
- He healeth the broken in heart and bindeth up their wounds. He telleth the number of the stars; He calleth them all by their names. Great is our Lord and of great power; His understanding is infinite.
- The Most High lifteth up the meek; He casteth the wicked down to the ground. Sing unto the Most High with thanksgiving, sing praise upon the harp unto our God, who covereth the heaven with clouds, who prepareth rain for the earth, who maketh grass to grow upon the mountains.
- He giveth to the beast his food and to the young ravens which cry. He delighteth not in the strength of the horse; He taketh not pleasure in the legs of a man.
- The Most High taketh pleasure in them that fear Him and in those that hope in His mercy. We are still talking about Israel here. He takes pleasure in those that fear Him, meaning those that keep His commandments. The way we know what fear is comes through the precepts.
  - **[Psalm 111:10](/bible/psalms/111#v10)**
    > <sup>[10](/bible/psalms/111#v10)</sup> The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments: his praise endureth for ever.

    The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom; those that fear the Lord are those that do His commandments.
  - **[Ecclesiasticus 15:1](/bible/sirach/15#v1)**  He that feareth the Lord will do good, and he that hath the knowledge of the law shall obtain her.  Those that fear the Lord will keep the commandments; that is what the fear of the Lord is.
- Those that hope in His mercy are going to keep His commandments. That is why faith without works is dead; you have to have faith and you have to have works. You hope in His mercy and you keep His commandments.

**[Psalm 147:12-20](/bible/psalms/147#v12)**

> <sup>[12](/bible/psalms/147#v12)</sup> Praise the Lord, O Jerusalem; praise thy God, O Zion.
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/psalms/147#v13)</sup> For he hath strengthened the bars of thy gates; he hath blessed thy children within thee.
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/psalms/147#v14)</sup> He maketh peace in thy borders, and filleth thee with the finest of the wheat.
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/psalms/147#v15)</sup> He sendeth forth his commandment upon earth: his word runneth very swiftly.
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/psalms/147#v16)</sup> He giveth snow like wool: he scattereth the hoarfrost like ashes.
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/psalms/147#v17)</sup> He casteth forth his ice like morsels: who can stand before his cold?
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/psalms/147#v18)</sup> He sendeth out his word, and melteth them: he causeth his wind to blow, and the waters flow.
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/psalms/147#v19)</sup> He sheweth his word unto Jacob, his statutes and his judgments unto Israel.
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/psalms/147#v20)</sup> He hath not dealt so with any nation: and as for his judgments, they have not known them. Praise ye the Lord.

- Praise the Most High, O Jerusalem; praise thy God, O Zion. Zion is another word for Israel, for Jerusalem, for the people. For He hath strengthened the bars of thy gates; He hath blessed thy children within thee.
- He maketh peace in thy borders and filleth thee with the finest of the wheat. He sendeth forth His commandment upon earth; His word runneth very swiftly. He giveth snow like wool; He scattereth the hoarfrost like ashes.
- He casteth forth His ice like morsels; who can stand before His cold? He sendeth out His word and melteth them; He causeth His wind to blow, and the waters flow.
- He sheweth His word unto Jacob. Jacob is Israel; Jacob is a forefather whose name was changed from Jacob to Israel. When the scriptures refer to a group of people as Jacob, they are referring to the nation of Israel.
- He sheweth His word unto Jacob, His statutes and His judgments unto Israel. He hath not dealt so with any nation, and as for His judgments they have not known them. All the other nations outside of Israel have not known the judgments the Most High wrote in His Bible, and they do not know the promises that come with them.
- None of this belongs to the other nations. No nation can just get up, get this Bible, and understand the judgments in it, because it is not for them. He only gave that to the Israelites.
